summary: Server only. A table for a board or card game: a board of rows and columns at a place in the world, pieces that stand on its cells and move between them, seats with a turn order, bets and save/load. You write the game's rules; the table does the rest. Every player of the table's dimension sees the pieces (they are props), and a player who joins later sees the board as it is. Near a free seat a player gets a 'Sit down' hint (U); seated, they point at a cell with the crosshair, or, with a camera shot of the table's or their seat's own, with the mouse pointer over the board as the game's dice players do, and click with mouse 1 or Enter; the arrow keys move the pointed cell as the player sees the board. The game's combat actions are held off while seated. The table's controls: { pointer: 'cursor' | 'crosshair' | 'keys', block: [game action names] } choose otherwise. Their game only sends the request: picking a piece raises tabletopPieceSelect and a move tabletopMoveRequest, which your handlers may refuse, and only then does the server move the piece. A player who stands up or leaves during a game forfeits it. Rows run along the table's y axis and columns along its x axis, both from 0. A resource's tables go when it stops.

create.summary: Makes a table. `position` is the middle of the board's top, where pieces stand; `rotation` turns it about the vertical axis (degrees, or a Quaternion); `dimension` defaults to the shared one. `board`: `rows` and `columns` (1 to 32, default 8), `cellSize` in metres (default 0.06), `height` (where pieces stand above `position`, default 0), `stackHeight` (how much higher each piece of a stack stands, default 0.01) and an optional `model` (a prop drawn as the board, with `scale`). `seats`: up to 8, each `{ position, rotation, side, animation, camera, chair, reach }`, where `animation` is `{ fragment, tags }` played while the player sits, `camera` a shot of the seat's own (or 'eyes': no shot, the game's own first-person view from the player's own eyes, wherever the seat puts the body), and `chair: true` means the game's own seat stands there (a chair or bench from SmartObject.spawn, or the level's): the player sits on it with the game's E and its walk up and sit-down, the table seats them when their game reports them seated within `reach` of `position` (0.9 m by default, up to 3: a tavern's long bench seats a player anywhere along it), and getting up from it stands them up; such a seat takes no `animation` and shows no Sit hint; while seated there W, A, S and D move the pointed cell instead of getting the player up, until Stand up (U) gives them back. `turnSeconds` (0, the default, for no limit) and `camera`, a shot as Camera.startShot takes it, shown to a seated player. A shot with `look` turns with the mouse within its limits: the crosshair then points and the game's own mouse look is held off.
create.exampleLua:
local Tabletop = kcds.world.Tabletop

local table = Tabletop.create({ position = { x = 1650.2, y = 2160.5, z = 36.1 }, rotation = 90, board = { model = "dice_board", rows = 8, columns = 8, cellSize = 0.07, height = 0.06 }, seats = { { position = { x = 1650.2, y = 2161.1, z = 35.6 }, rotation = 180, side = "white" }, { position = { x = 1650.2, y = 2159.9, z = 35.6 }, rotation = 0, side = "black" } }, turnSeconds = 60 })
create.exampleCs: var table = Tabletop.Create(new { position = new { x = 1650.2, y = 2160.5, z = 36.1 }, rotation = 90, board = new { model = "dice_board", rows = 8, columns = 8, cellSize = 0.07, height = 0.06 }, seats = new object[] { new { position = new { x = 1650.2, y = 2161.1, z = 35.6 }, rotation = 180, side = "white" }, new { position = new { x = 1650.2, y = 2159.9, z = 35.6 }, rotation = 0, side = "black" } }, turnSeconds = 60 });

all.summary: Every table, or those of one dimension.

getById.summary: The table with this id, or null.
getById.exampleLua:
local table = kcds.world.Tabletop.getById(1)
if table then
  print(table.state)
end

id.summary: The table's id, unique while the server runs.

exists.summary: Whether the table is still there (destroy, or its resource stopped, removes it).
exists.exampleLua:
if not table.exists then
  print("the table is gone")
end

position.summary: Where the middle of the board's top is.

rotation.example: const along = table.rotation.rotateVector(new kcds.math.Vector3(1, 0, 0)); // the columns' direction
rotation.exampleCs: var along = table.Rotation.RotateVector(new Vector3(1, 0, 0)); // the columns' direction

dimension.summary: The dimension the table is in; only its players see and use it.

rows.summary: How many rows the board has.

columns.summary: How many columns the board has.
columns.exampleLua:
for column = 0, table.columns - 1 do
  print(table:pieceAt({ row = 0, column = column }))
end

pieces.summary: The pieces on the board, in the order they were added.
pieces.exampleLua:
local white = 0
for _, piece in ipairs(table.pieces) do
  if piece.side == "white" then
    white = white + 1
  end
end

seats.summary: The seats, as { index, side, player }, with player null for a free one.
seats.exampleLua:
local free = 0
for _, seat in ipairs(table.seats) do
  if seat.player == nil then
    free = free + 1
  end
end

state.summary: 'playing' while a game is on (start to finish), else 'idle'.
state.exampleLua:
local everyoneSits = true
for _, seat in ipairs(table.seats) do
  everyoneSits = everyoneSits and seat.player ~= nil
end
if table.state == "idle" and everyoneSits then
  table:start()
end

turn.summary: The seat whose turn it is, -1 when no game is on. While a game is on, only that seat's player can pick and move pieces.
turn.exampleLua: local mover = (table.turn >= 0 and table:playerAt(table.turn) or nil)

pot.summary: How much bets put on the table, in units of their item.

cellPosition.summary: Where a cell's middle is in the world. Throws a RangeError for a cell off the board.

cellAt.summary: The cell under a position, or null when it is off the board.

addPiece.summary: Puts a piece on a cell, on top of any already there. `model` is a prop model (the game's or one your resource ships, see Props); `side` and `data` are yours (whose piece, a king's crown, a card's value); `rotation` turns it on the board (degrees); `scale` sizes it; `visibleTo` shows it to one player or a list only (a hand of cards). At most 256 pieces on a table.

params.options: { model, cell, side, data, rotation, scale, visibleTo }.

addPiece.example: const stone = table.addPiece({ model: 'dicebadge_balatro_badge_gold', cell: [0, 1], side: 'white' });
addPiece.exampleLua: local stone = table:addPiece({ model = "dicebadge_balatro_badge_gold", cell = { 0, 1 }, side = "white" })
addPiece.exampleCs: var stone = table.AddPiece(new { model = "dicebadge_balatro_badge_gold", cell = new[] { 0, 1 }, side = "white" });

piecesAt.summary: The pieces on a cell, bottom first.

pieceAt.summary: The top piece of a cell, or null for an empty one.
pieceAt.exampleLua:
if table:pieceAt({ row = 4, column = 4 }) == nil then
  print("the middle is free")
end

highlight.summary: Marks cells, for some players (`players`) or everyone, in a colour (`color`, 0xAARRGGBB, a soft gold by default) and a `style`: 'frame' (the default), a border with a faint inside; 'fill', the whole cell tinted; 'dot', a round dot in the middle, as for the cells a piece may go to. The players' games draw the marks flat on the board. A table keeps at most 64 `highlight` calls' marks; the table marks a player's picked piece by itself.

params.cells: A cell, or a list of them.

highlight.exampleCs: table.Highlight(new object[] { new[] { 2, 3 }, new[] { 2, 5 } }, new { players = new[] { player }, color = 0xff60c060, style = "dot" });

clearHighlight.summary: Removes the marks for these players, or every mark.

params.players: Optional: a Player or a list.

sit.summary: Seats a player, as their own request from the 'Sit down' hint does: they move to the seat, its animation plays and the table's camera shot starts. False for a taken seat, a player who already sits at the table, one in another dimension, or a tabletopSit handler that refused.
sit.exampleLua:
kcds.core.Events.on("playerCommand", function(player, command)
  if command == "play" then
    table:sit(player, table.seats:findIndex(function(seat) return seat.player == nil end))
  end
end)

stand.summary: Stands a player up, as the 'Stand up' hint does. A player who stands during a game forfeits it. False for one who does not sit here.

seatOf.summary: The seat a player sits on, -1 for none.
seatOf.example:
const seat = table.seatOf(player);
const mine = seat >= 0 ? table.seats[seat].side : null;
seatOf.exampleLua:
local seat = table:seatOf(player)
local mine = (seat >= 0 and table.seats[seat].side or nil)
seatOf.exampleCs:
var seat = table.SeatOf(player);
var mine = seat >= 0 ? table.Seats[(int)seat]["side"] : default;

playerAt.summary: The player on a seat, or null.

start.summary: Starts a game: the turn goes to `turn` (default the first taken seat), with tabletopStart and tabletopTurn. Throws when nobody sits.
start.exampleLua:
kcds.core.Events.on("tabletopSit", function(table)
  setTimeout(function()
    if table.state ~= "idle" then
      return
    end
    for _, seat in ipairs(table.seats) do
      if not seat.player then
        return
      end
    end
    table:start()
  end, 0)
end)

nextTurn.summary: Passes the turn to the next taken seat, with tabletopTurn, and starts its timer. Returns that seat. Throws when no game is on.

finish.summary: Ends the game with tabletopEnd: the winner (a seat or a Player) takes the pot; with none (null) everyone gets back what they bet.

params.winner: A seat, a Player, or null for none.

bet.summary: Takes `amount` of an item (`item`, default 'money') from every seated player for the pot: all or nothing, so if one cannot pay, all get theirs back and it answers false.

params.amount: Units each player puts in, 1 to 1000000.

bet.exampleLua:
if not (table:bet(20):await()) then
  kcds.core.Chat.sendToAll("Not everyone can pay the stake.")
end

clear.summary: Takes every piece off the board, for a new game.

save.summary: The board as data, JSON you can store: its pieces (model, cell, side, data, turn and who sees them) and the turn.
save.exampleLua:
kcds.core.Events.on("resourceStop", function()
  local text = json.encode(table:save())
  print("board saved, " .. tostring(#text) .. " characters")
end)

load.summary: Puts the board back as save() gave it, in place of the pieces it has now.

createDeck.summary: Lays a deck of pieces on the table that its players hold in their hands (a TabletopDeck): the 52 playing cards by default, `jokers: true` for 54, `ranks` for a shorter one (['7', '8', '9', 'T', 'J', 'Q', 'K', 'A'] for Prší's and Mariáš's 32), or `pieces`, your own ids, with their models in `models` (a folder of your resource's stream, objects/kcds/<resource>/<folder>, holding <id>.cgf and back.cgf, lower case). `position` { x, y } is the stack's place from the board's middle, `height` the table top's above the board, `playPile` the pile played pieces land on ('table', at `playPosition`), `holdAnimation` the animation a holder sits in ({ fragment, tags }; the game's dice players' sitting by default, the one the hold is made for; null for none) and `actions` the labels of the holder's draw, pass and look keys (see setActions). At most 4 decks on a table.

params.options: Optional: { pieces, ranks, jokers, models, position, height, playPile, playPosition, holdAnimation, actions }.

createDeck.example: const deck = table.createDeck({ ranks: ['7', '8', '9', 'T', 'J', 'Q', 'K', 'A'], actions: { draw: 'Draw a card' } });
createDeck.exampleLua: local deck = table:createDeck({ ranks = { "7", "8", "9", "T", "J", "Q", "K", "A" }, actions = { draw = "Draw a card" } })
createDeck.exampleCs: var deck = table.CreateDeck(new { ranks = new[] { "7", "8", "9", "T", "J", "Q", "K", "A" }, actions = new { draw = "Draw a card" } });

lookCloser.summary: Steps a seated player through the close looks (their own key C): first at the pieces in their hand, when they hold a deck's pieces face up, then at the table as the game's dice players have it, then their seat's view again.

destroy.summary: Removes the table: its players stand up (reason 'removed'), a game ends without a winner and its pieces and board go.
